title: From patterns to processes
text:
About
Ecological systems can respond to stress gradually, nonlinearly or through abrupt shifts between states. Many methods now exist to detect such changes, to measure resilience and to anticipate transitions, but it is often unclear which of them can be applied to the data that ecologists actually have. The meeting asks whether resilience can be quantified and abrupt shifts anticipated from empirical data, and what current methods can and cannot deliver.
Four questions frame the meeting:

Detection. How common are abrupt shifts in ecological time series, and why are they missed?
Measurement. Which resilience metrics can be estimated from data?
Mechanism. Can interactions and causality explain why a system shifts?
Anticipation. Do early-warning signals and machine learning work on real data?

title: From patterns to processes
text:
Tentative programme

Monday 22 March: ecoFAST tutorial
A one-day practical course on ecoFAST, an R package for detecting abrupt shifts and quantifying resilience in ecological data. The morning introduces the principles of the methods and the afternoon is devoted to hands-on practice. The tutorial requires registration.


Tuesday 23 March: colloquium
A day of invited talks, open to all. Each method talk is followed by a case study that applies or tests such a method. The talks are grouped in two sessions:

Detecting shifts and measuring resilience
Mechanisms and anticipation

The day ends with a panel discussion.
